pages.text: "Strawberry jam! I want to eat that whole jar!" Rudi the hungry squirrel ran to the kitchen shelf. Steam drifted from the jam jar. Rudi gulped.

Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, scooped one spoonful with a big wooden spoon and spread it on Rudi's bread. "Lunch soup will be ready soon. Just this much jam." Rudi swallowed the bread in three bites and stared at the jar.
Grandma went to the stream for water. Rudi plunged the spoon into the jar, again and again. "Just a little more, a little more..."
The spoon scraped the bottom. Not a strawberry was left. Rudi's tummy bulged like a drum. Their heavy tail drooped onto the floor.

The lunch bell rang, and soup came to the table. Rudi's tummy ached, so they couldn't take even a spoonful. Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, emptied their bowl. "Rudi, aren't you eating soup?"
Grandma set the empty jar beside the big spoon. "This one jar has to last until strawberries grow again. One spoonful, then lid on!" Grandma pressed the lid with her palm to show Rudi.
Ppino called from the door. "Let's go out and play!" Curled beside the stove, Rudi only shook their head. A sore tummy kept Rudi inside all afternoon.
The next morning, Grandma opened a new jam jar. Rudi took just one spoonful, spread it on bread, then shut the lid firmly. Rudi wrapped their tail around their body and held back. "Done!"
At lunch, Rudi ate two whole bowls of hot soup. "One, just one spoonful! Two, lid on! Three, meals first!" Two empty bowls sat side by side before Rudi.
When the evening bell rang, Grandma held Rudi's cheeks in both hands. Eat a little, and there is jam left and a comfortable tummy. "One spoonful, then lid on!" Rudi pressed the jar lid firmly shut.
